editorial: You never step into a relationship drama quite like Bight, where every whisper feels like a shared secret. By dismantling the illusion of fidelity, the director reimagines open couples as a spiral of passion and paranoia, refusing the easy truce of conventional love movies. A single scene where the camera lingers on a cracked mirror as the protagonist confronts reflected lies showcases the film's deft blend of visceral intimacy and subtle dread. If you thrive on psychological thrillers that tease your guilty conscience, Bight will keep you huddled in the dark.
targetAudience: Ideal for fans of psychological thrillers that blur the line between desire and dread.
similarMovies: Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind
